text:
## Content

Overview This article describes the general request process for onboarding a new product into the invoicing catalog. Steps Submit a product onboarding request with product name, category, and applicable tax code. The Configuration team reviews and adds the product to the master data table. Allow up to 2 business days for the product to appear across all invoicing screens. Note If a newly added product does not appear where expected after this window, raise a support ticket rather than resubmitting the request.

title: Enterprise Application UI and Functionality Issues - Overview
text:
### Overview
This article provides diagnostic procedures and escalation guidelines for Enterprise Application functionality issues, such as product dropdowns not populating, invoice checkboxes not getting ticked, form submission errors, and portal rendering defects.

title: Enterprise Application UI and Functionality Issues - Common Symptoms & Diagnostics
text:
### Common Symptoms & Diagnostics
1. **Dropdown Not Showing Products**:
   - Newly requested or unconfigured products (such as 4K Webcam Pro or peripheral accessories) do not appear in the invoice or procurement dropdown.
   - Root Cause: Product is disabled in master catalog configuration (`backend/catalog_config.json`) or catalog synchronization is pending.
   - Resolution: Must be enabled in master catalog configuration (`show_in_invoice_dropdown: true`) by Support Engineering. Client-side browser refresh or cache clear will not resolve this.

title: Enterprise Application UI and Functionality Issues - Common Symptoms & Diagnostics
text:
2. **Invoice Checkbox Not Getting Ticked**:
   - Checkbox controls (e.g., compliance confirmation, bulk selection, invoice certification) do not respond to clicks or fail to toggle state.
   - Root Cause: Frontend UI event-handling defect or form validation state locking in `employee_portal.html`.
   - Resolution: Requires frontend code patch by Support Engineering.

title: Enterprise Application UI and Functionality Issues - Common Symptoms & Diagnostics
text:
3. **Application Crashes & Un-operational Functionality**:
   - Calculation errors (such as Currency Tax Aggregation crash) or non-operational workflow buttons.
   - Root Cause: Backend API calculation error or missing database normalization schema.
   - SLA & Timeline: See SOP-ENG-004 for multi-file architectural defect estimation.

title: Enterprise Application UI and Functionality Issues - Escalation Protocol
text:
### Escalation Protocol
- When an employee reports an application-level defect or un-operational functionality:
  1. The Self Help Agent scans Confluence knowledge base articles.
  2. The agent explains with empathy that this is an enterprise application defect that cannot be fixed through client-side settings.
  3. The issue is escalated to Level 2 Support Engineer Alex Turner.
  4. The escalation attaches the live conversation chat link so the engineer can review the context and chat with the employee.
  5. Remote desktop access (MeshCentral) is NOT required for enterprise application bugs.
  6. The Support Engineer asks the Code Analysis Agent to investigate the application GitHub repository, apply the code change, and execute the CI/CD pipeline for deployment to AWS ECS Fargate.

section: SOP-ENG-004: Multi-File Architectural Defect Estimation & SLA Guidelines
text:
# SOP-ENG-004: Multi-File Architectural Defect Estimation & SLA Guidelines

**Confluence Space:** Engineering Standard Operating Procedures (ENG-SOP)
**Document ID:** SOP-ENG-004 | **Category:** Technical Estimation & SLA Standards
**Last Updated:** 2026-09-30 | **Author:** IT Architecture & Support Engineering

title: SOP Multi File Architectural Defect Estimation - 1. Overview & Purpose
text:
## 1. Overview & Purpose
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) governs technical effort calculation, cross-file impact analysis, and customer SLA communication when an enterprise application failure is caused by an architectural defect spanning multiple system layers (e.g. database schema, backend computation APIs, and frontend views).

title: SOP Multi File Architectural Defect Estimation - 2. Classification of Multi-File Architectural Defects
text:
## 2. Classification of Multi-File Architectural Defects
A defect is classified as an **Architectural Multi-File Defect** when resolving it requires coordinated changes across two or more independent architectural boundaries:
1. **Data Persistence Layer:** Altering database models, table schemas, adding foreign keys, migration scripts, or data backfilling.
2. **Business Logic & API Layer:** Refactoring core computation services, currency conversion engines, tax calculation logic, or API contracts.
3. **User Interface / Presentation Layer:** Updating templates, client-side validation, error boundaries, or report generation views.

title: SOP Multi File Architectural Defect Estimation - Example Defect: Currency Tax Aggregation Error
section: Example Defect: Currency Tax Aggregation Error
text:
### Example Defect: Currency Tax Aggregation Error
* **Symptom:** Application crashes when attempting to aggregate line-item taxes across multi-currency invoices (USD, EUR, GBP) without an exchange rate normalization schema.
* **Impacted Layers:**
  - `backend/database/models.py`: Requires adding multi-currency exchange rate and normalized tax columns to `Invoice` and `Product` models.
  - `backend/routers/enterprise.py`: Requires implementing exchange rate lookup and multi-currency tax aggregation computation algorithms.
  - `frontend/templates/employee_portal.html`: Requires updating the tax reconciliation reporting interface, currency pickers, and exception handling.

title: SOP Multi File Architectural Defect Estimation - 3. Standard Estimation & Effort Benchmark Matrix
text:
## 3. Standard Estimation & Effort Benchmark Matrix
For architectural defects requiring schema migration, calculation engine refactoring, and UI updates, the standard engineering estimate is strictly calculated as follows:

title: SOP Multi File Architectural Defect Estimation - 3. Standard Estimation & Effort Benchmark Matrix
text:
| Phase | Scope of Work | Standard Benchmark |
| :--- | :--- | :---: |
| **Phase 1: Database Migration** | Schema definition updates (`models.py`), migration generation, historical data backfill script, rollback validation. | **1 Business Day** |
| **Phase 2: Backend Calculation** | Implementing currency exchange lookup service, updating tax aggregation logic, unit tests in `enterprise.py`. | **1 Business Day** |
| **Phase 3: Frontend Reporting** | Tax reconciliation view enhancements, currency selection, error boundaries in `employee_portal.html`. | **1 Business Day** |
| **Phase 4: QA & Deployment** | End-to-end integration testing, financial accuracy regression, staging sign-off, and production deployment. | **1 Business Day** |
| **TOTAL ESTIMATED TIMELINE** | **Comprehensive Multi-File Resolution** | **4 Business Days** |

title: SOP Multi File Architectural Defect Estimation - 4. Support Engineer (L2/L3) Decision & Communication Protocol
text:
## 4. Support Engineer (L2/L3) Decision & Communication Protocol
1. **Tool-Assisted Discovery:** The Support Engineer invokes the Code Analysis Agent (SmartFix) to trace affected files in the repository and compute the baseline effort.
2. **Engineer Decision & Validation:** The Support Engineer (Alex Turner) reviews the agent's findings, validates that the 4-day benchmark aligns with current sprint capacity, and personally confirms the timeline.
3. **Direct Customer ETA Communication:** The Support Engineer personally notifies the reporting employee (Maya) via the live chat session with the official 4 business day ETA and explanation of the multi-file scope.
4. **Jira Lifecycle Management:** 
   - The Jira ticket MUST remain **OPEN** in status `In Progress` / `L2 Confirmed`.
   - The ticket must NOT be closed until the development team completes deployment and the fix is verified in production.

title: Understanding tax codes in the invoicing system - Content
text: ## Content

title: Understanding tax codes in the invoicing system - Content
text: Overview Tax codes determine how tax is calculated and reported for each invoice, based on GST (Goods and Services Tax) brackets. Current tax brackets GST 5%: Applies to select essential product categories. GST 12%: Applies to standard mid-tier products. GST 18%: The default rate for most catalog items. GST 28% (New Category): Used for newly onboarded product categories. Invoices using this bracket require Remarks explaining the classification, for audit purposes. If you're unsure which code to use Check the product's category listing, or raise a query with the Finance Configuration team.

title: Uploading client tax documents - Content
text:
## Content

Overview Each client may have specific tax documentation on file, such as a tax exemption certificate or GST registration certificate for their jurisdiction. Steps Select the client before uploading their document - documents are tied to the specific client, not the invoice. Upload the relevant certificate in the Tax Document field on the Raise Invoice screen. If you switch to a different client, you must upload that client's own document - a previous client's file does not carry over. Note Missing or mismatched tax documentation may delay invoice approval.

title: Windows 11 Microphone  Camera Privacy Permissions Troubleshooting - Reported Symptoms
text:
## Reported Symptoms

* Microphone not working in video conferencing apps (Teams, Zoom, Meet)
* Camera shows black/blocked in video calls
* Windows says microphone access is blocked or denied
* App says 'We can't access your microphone'
* Camera privacy indicator shows access is off
* Audio routing not working — can hear but can't be heard
* Microphone works in some apps but not others
* Windows 11 privacy settings blocking mic or camera
* Headset microphone not detected in meeting apps
* Camera permission denied by operating system

title: Windows 11 Microphone  Camera Privacy Permissions Troubleshooting - Troubleshooting Steps
text: ## Troubleshooting Steps

title: Windows 11 Microphone  Camera Privacy Permissions Troubleshooting - Step 1: Check Windows Privacy Settings for Microphone
section: Step 1: Check Windows Privacy Settings for Microphone
text:
### Step 1: Check Windows Privacy Settings for Microphone

Windows 11 has privacy controls that can block apps from accessing the microphone. These settings are OS-level and must be changed manually through the Windows Settings UI — they cannot be safely overridden by background scripts as it would violate operating system security policies.

title: Windows 11 Microphone  Camera Privacy Permissions Troubleshooting - Step 1: Check Windows Privacy Settings for Microphone
section: Step 1: Check Windows Privacy Settings for Microphone
text:
**Instructions:**
1. Open Windows Settings (Win + I).
2. Navigate to Privacy & Security > Microphone.
3. Ensure 'Microphone access' is turned ON.
4. Ensure 'Let apps access your microphone' is turned ON.
5. Scroll down and ensure the specific app (Teams, Zoom, etc.) has microphone access enabled.
6. If using a desktop app, ensure 'Let desktop apps access your microphone' is turned ON at the bottom.

title: Windows 11 Microphone  Camera Privacy Permissions Troubleshooting - Step 1: Check Windows Privacy Settings for Microphone
section: Step 1: Check Windows Privacy Settings for Microphone
text: > **Note:** These privacy settings are protected by Windows security policies and MUST be changed through the UI by the user or a support technician. Automated scripts should never silently override OS privacy controls.

title: Windows 11 Microphone  Camera Privacy Permissions Troubleshooting - Step 2: Check Windows Privacy Settings for Camera
section: Step 2: Check Windows Privacy Settings for Camera
text:
### Step 2: Check Windows Privacy Settings for Camera

Similar to microphone, Windows 11 has privacy controls for camera access that must be manually configured.

**Instructions:**
1. Open Windows Settings (Win + I).
2. Navigate to Privacy & Security > Camera.
3. Ensure 'Camera access' is turned ON.
4. Ensure 'Let apps access your camera' is turned ON.
5. Scroll down and ensure the specific app has camera access enabled.
6. If using a desktop app, ensure 'Let desktop apps access your camera' is turned ON.

title: Windows 11 Microphone  Camera Privacy Permissions Troubleshooting - Step 2: Check Windows Privacy Settings for Camera
section: Step 2: Check Windows Privacy Settings for Camera
text: > **Note:** Camera privacy settings are OS-level security controls and must not be overridden by scripts.

title: Windows 11 Microphone  Camera Privacy Permissions Troubleshooting - Step 3: Check Sound Settings and Default Device
section: Step 3: Check Sound Settings and Default Device
text:
### Step 3: Check Sound Settings and Default Device

The wrong audio input/output device may be selected as the default, or the microphone volume may be muted.

**Instructions:**
1. Right-click the speaker icon in the taskbar and select 'Sound settings'.
2. Under 'Input', check that the correct microphone is selected.
3. Click on the microphone and ensure the volume is not at 0.
4. Test the microphone by speaking — the input level indicator should move.
5. Under 'Output', verify the correct speakers/headset is selected.

title: Windows 11 Microphone  Camera Privacy Permissions Troubleshooting - Step 4: Run Windows Audio Troubleshooter
text:
### Step 4: Run Windows Audio Troubleshooter

Windows has a built-in troubleshooter that can detect and fix common audio problems.

**Instructions:**
1. Open Windows Settings (Win + I).
2. Go to System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters.
3. Find 'Recording Audio' and click 'Run'.
4. Follow the on-screen instructions.
5. Restart the affected app after the troubleshooter completes.

title: Windows 11 Microphone  Camera Privacy Permissions Troubleshooting - Step 5: Escalate to L2 Support — Remote Desktop Session
section: Step 5: Escalate to L2 Support — Remote Desktop Session
text:
### Step 5: Escalate to L2 Support — Remote Desktop Session

If the user is unable to navigate Windows privacy settings or the issue persists after manual checks, escalate to a Level 2 support technician who can connect via a secure, time-limited remote desktop session to visually resolve the issue.

**Instructions:**
This step is handled by the AI — it will create a secure 30-minute remote desktop sharing link for a support technician to connect and resolve the issue visually.

title: Windows 11 Microphone  Camera Privacy Permissions Troubleshooting - Step 5: Escalate to L2 Support — Remote Desktop Session
section: Step 5: Escalate to L2 Support — Remote Desktop Session
text: > **Note:** A human technician will connect via a 30-minute self-expiring web remote desktop link. No client software is needed. The link automatically revokes after the time window.

title: Windows 11 Microphone  Camera Privacy Permissions Troubleshooting - Escalation Guidelines
text:
## Escalation Guidelines

Issues involving Windows OS-level privacy settings (microphone/camera permissions) and audio routing configurations require visual human intervention. The AI should identify this boundary and open an L2 support ticket with an ephemeral remote desktop sharing link for a technician to resolve the issue.

text:
# Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide

**Confluence URL:** https://agnishpaul2002.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SELFHELP/pages/5341202
**Page ID:** 5341202
**Document ID:** KB-ZOOM-001 | **Category:** Video Conferencing | **Application:** Zoom
**Last Updated:** 2026-09-21 | **Author:** IT Support Team

**Tags:** zoom, video conferencing, freezing, crashing, audio, video, camera, microphone, cache, not working, can't join, meeting, lag, slow, black screen, screen share, reinstall, uninstall, corrupt, error 10003, crash on launch

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Preliminary Assessment
text:
## Preliminary Assessment

Before proceeding directly to cache clearing or reinstallation, it is essential to ask the user diagnostic questions to identify whether the crash is triggered by corrupted temporary cache files, GPU hardware acceleration conflicts, or background process locks. In the vast majority of cases where Zoom crashes abruptly during launch or joining calls without a system hardware fault, corrupted local AppData cache files (CEF webcache, meeting session data, and dump logs) are the primary culprit.

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Diagnostic Questions
text:
## Diagnostic Questions

* When exactly does the issue occur? (e.g., Immediately upon launching Zoom, during sign-in, when clicking 'Join Meeting', or when starting video/screen sharing?)
* Do you see any error messages or error codes (such as Error 10003, Error 3000, or a Windows application crash notification), or does Zoom close abruptly without warning?
* Did this problem start happening recently (for example, following a recent Zoom client update, Windows update, or system reboot)?

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Reported Symptoms
text: ## Reported Symptoms

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Reported Symptoms
text:
* Zoom application freezes or becomes unresponsive upon opening
* Zoom crashes unexpectedly during or before meetings
* Zoom crashes immediately when joining a meeting or starting video
* Zoom window turns white or black and closes without an error message
* Audio not working in Zoom (can't hear or be heard)
* Video/camera not working in Zoom or showing blank display
* Unable to join Zoom meetings with connection timeout
* Zoom is running slow, dropping frames, or lagging severely
* Screen sharing fails or causes the application to terminate
* Zoom login issues or authentication session tokens corrupted
* Zoom updates failing or corrupt installation state
* Zoom keeps crashing even after simple restart

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Troubleshooting Steps
text: ## Troubleshooting Steps

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Step 1: Clear Zoom Application Cache
text:
### Step 1: Clear Zoom Application Cache

Zoom stores session caches, CEF webcache, thumbnails, avatar caches, and local meeting states in AppData\Local\Zoom and AppData\Roaming\Zoom. Over time or after improper application termination, these files become corrupted, causing instant crashes when Zoom tries to initialize the UI or join meetings. Clearing the cache purges these corrupted temporary files while preserving the core executable, forcing Zoom to rebuild fresh configuration databases on next launch.

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Step 1: Clear Zoom Application Cache
text:
**Instructions:**
1. Close Zoom completely (check the system tray to ensure no background Zoom processes are running).
2. Press Win+R, type '%appdata%\Zoom' and press Enter.
3. Delete the 'data', 'logs', 'report', and 'dump' folders (do not touch 'bin' or 'uninstall' folders).
4. Press Win+R, type '%localappdata%\Zoom' and press Enter, then delete 'webcache' and 'temp'.
5. Also check '%temp%' and remove any temporary files prefixed with 'Zoom'.
6. Relaunch Zoom and sign back in.

> **Note:** This will sign you out of Zoom. You will need to log in again after clearing the cache.

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Step 2: Clean Reinstall Zoom
text:
### Step 2: Clean Reinstall Zoom

If clearing the cache does not resolve the issue, a full clean reinstall removes all Zoom components (including potentially corrupted binaries, DLLs, and registry entries) and installs a fresh copy of the latest version from the Microsoft Store or official package repository. This resolves deep binary corruption, version conflicts, and persistent crashes.

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Step 2: Clean Reinstall Zoom
text:
**Instructions:**
1. Close Zoom completely.
2. Open Settings > Apps > Installed Apps.
3. Find 'Zoom' or 'Zoom Workplace', click Uninstall.
4. After uninstall, delete leftover folders: %appdata%\Zoom and %localappdata%\Zoom.
5. Download and install the latest Zoom Workplace package.
6. Relaunch Zoom and log in.

> **Note:** This will completely remove Zoom and all its settings/data. The application will be reinstalled fresh. Custom settings will need to be reconfigured.

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Step 3: Restart Zoom Application and Background Processes
section: Step 3: Restart Zoom Application and Background Processes
text:
### Step 3: Restart Zoom Application and Background Processes

A hanging ZoomOpener or CptHost process in Task Manager can lock Zoom data files, preventing a new instance from opening properly.

**Instructions:**
1. Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager.
2. Look for any 'Zoom', 'Zoom Meetings', 'ZoomOpener', or 'CptHost' processes.
3. Select each and click 'End Task'.
4. Reopen Zoom from the Start Menu.

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Step 4: Check Network Stability & Firewall
text:
### Step 4: Check Network Stability & Firewall

Zoom requires an active and stable network connection with open UDP ports. Packet loss or aggressive proxy filters can cause crashes during the meeting handshake.

**Instructions:**
1. Test your internet connection by navigating to a web browser.
2. Run a speed test (minimum 3-5 Mbps recommended for video calls).
3. If connected to a VPN or proxy, temporarily disconnect and test Zoom directly.
4. If on Wi-Fi, try connecting to a 5GHz band or ethernet cable.

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Step 5: Disable Hardware Acceleration in Zoom Video Settings
section: Step 5: Disable Hardware Acceleration in Zoom Video Settings
text:
### Step 5: Disable Hardware Acceleration in Zoom Video Settings

Incompatible or outdated GPU display drivers frequently cause Zoom to crash or display a black/white screen when opening video.

**Instructions:**
1. Open Zoom Settings (gear icon in the top right).
2. Click 'Video' in the left sidebar, then click 'Advanced'.
3. Uncheck 'Enable hardware acceleration for video processing' and 'Enable hardware acceleration for receiving video'.
4. Restart Zoom.

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Step 6: Verify Audio and Camera Privacy Permissions
section: Step 6: Verify Audio and Camera Privacy Permissions
text:
### Step 6: Verify Audio and Camera Privacy Permissions

Windows Privacy Settings can block Zoom from accessing microphones and cameras, which can lead to application crashes when starting meeting media.

**Instructions:**
1. Open Windows Settings > Privacy & Security.
2. Under App Permissions, select 'Camera' and ensure 'Let desktop apps access your camera' is enabled for Zoom.
3. Select 'Microphone' and ensure 'Let desktop apps access your microphone' is enabled for Zoom.
4. Relaunch Zoom.

title: Zoom Application Troubleshooting Guide - Escalation Guidelines
text:
## Escalation Guidelines

If preliminary troubleshooting, cache clearing, and clean reinstallation do not resolve the issue, escalate to a human Support Engineer for visual remote desktop inspection. The engineer can review Windows Event Viewer logs (Application crash events 1000/1001), inspect driver compatibility, or debug system-level group policies.
